case.description: Create a reusable joint between two square rods in a tabletop pointer frame. The joint must let the operator exchange either rod while restoring the pointer's marked position without altering the rods.
case.valued_outcome: After five exchanges of each rod, the pointer returns within a 2 mm target circle and remains there during a supplied 10 N lateral load for ten seconds; each exchange takes less than forty seconds.
hard_constraints: No drilling, adhesive or permanent marks on either rod.
Joint envelope must fit inside a 90 mm cube.
Only hand-operated assembly and adjustment are permitted.
No component may fall free during an exchange.
resources: Two 400 mm square rods, measured sides 19 mm and 20 mm, plus one pointer and marked base.
Six plywood pieces each 80 by 40 by 6 mm, eight M5 bolts with nuts, four washers, two 150 mm elastic loops and 0.5 m of cord.
Hand drill for plywood only, saw, file, screwdriver and ruler.
One hundred minutes for fabrication and twenty minutes for testing.
observations: The current loose joint lets the pointer move 7 mm under the load.
Rod ends are square within the supplied 1 mm measurement resolution.
Awkward observation: the visually tighter rod fit returned 3 mm farther from the target after exchange than the looser fit in two supplied trials.

openings.delta: Attack the dependence on seating surviving movable-plate tightening. openings.prediction: Nearest rival: pocket compliance, rather than seating disturbance, explains poor return. Closure-induced pointer movement that decreases with preload, followed by similar loaded deflection, favors disturbed seating. Comparable closure movement or return scatter defeats this branch; equal excessive loaded drift favors inadequate pocket stiffness. These predictions are unverified.
openings.probe: Build one configuration within 100 minutes, first checking 90 mm envelope, hand-only operation and cord-retained hardware. Within twenty minutes perform twelve exchanges, six per rod position, alternating ordinary seating and elastic-preloaded closure; use the 18 mm rod for the last two exchanges of the smaller position. Record pointer position immediately before and after tightening, then after removing preload, and exchange duration. Apply four ten-second 10 N loads across both procedures and rod sizes. Check every final return and loaded position against the 2 mm circle; fail any forty-second exchange or freed component. This is a diagnostic probe, with only three exchanges per procedure per rod, not independent complete validation of both procedures.
assumptions: Incumbent pocket geometry fits six plywood pieces and eight bolts; no extra hardware is available.
Loops can supply directional preload inside the envelope without obstructing exchange or leaving a permanent rod mark.
Ruler and target permit useful closure-shift measurements; precision and plywood stiffness remain unknown.
